title: Jonah and the Kitchen
premise: Paloma Coldharbour inherited her family's vineyard with more debt than vines, and the only way to keep it is a buyout offer from her uncle that comes with humiliating strings. To survive the Coldharbour reunion where the deal will be signed, she hires Jonah Marsh, a quiet line cook with a rehearsed confession he's carried for ten years, to pose as her boyfriend. What begins as theater turns real by dessert, but Jonah's secret — that he once testified against the Coldharbour patriarch and lost everything for it — surfaces just as Paloma discovers the buyout is a scheme to strip the land. Choosing justice over safety, the two expose her uncle at the harvest gala, and Paloma keeps the vineyard not through the deal but through the community they rallied, ending with a real first date ten years overdue.
about_author: Casper Delacroix is the pseudonym of a former restaurant critic who spent a decade covering vineyard towns and the families who run them. They write romances about people who mistake duty for love and only notice the difference at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She walks the frost-bitten rows of Coldharbour Vineyard, tallying what's left: three working fields, a mortgage, and an uncle's buyout offer sitting on her desk. A letter summons her to the family reunion where the deal must be signed. Emotional beat: exhausted defiance — she'll attend, but on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Cook Who Waits
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Working the line at a bistro in town, Jonah recognizes Paloma when she comes in for a late dinner — the girl from the trial ten years ago who never saw his face. His rehearsed confession sits unspoken, as it always has. Emotional beat: longing sharpened by cowardice.

chapters.title: An Indecent Proposal, Properly Worded
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Over dessert, she impulsively asks the cook if he'll be her boyfriend for one weekend. Jonah, stunned that fate has opened the door, agrees before thinking through what standing in that house will cost him. Emotional beat: reckless hope disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Rehearsals
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They build the fake history in Paloma's kitchen over two nights — how they met, first kiss, inside jokes. The invented details keep colliding with real ones. Emotional beat: intimacy arriving through fiction, both pretending not to notice.

chapters.title: The Gates of Coldharbour
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Arrival at the estate: her uncle Ambrose all charm, her aunt measuring Paloma's 'boyfriend' like livestock, cousins trading barbs. Jonah plays his role flawlessly, which unsettles her — he seems too comfortable in enemy territory. Emotional beat: performance hardening into armor.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the reunion dinner, Paloma's hand finds his under the table and neither lets go. Ambrose toasts the buyout, and Jonah watches the patriarch's lawyer — the same man from the trial — and nearly chokes. Emotional beat: the fake date curdling into something he can't control.

chapters.title: Cellar Truths
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Jonah pulls her into the wine cellar to escape the party, and instead of a kiss, he almost tells her everything — then a cousin interrupts. Paloma catches the half-sentence and feels the shape of a lie she can't name. Emotional beat: trust with a hairline crack.

chapters.title: The Fine Print
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She reads Ambrose's contract properly for the first time: the buyout transfers water rights permanently, leaving the vineyard unviable if she ever defaults. It's not rescue; it's a trap. Emotional beat: cold clarity replacing desperation.

chapters.title: What Jonah Lost
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Backstory chapter: ten years ago, young Jonah testified against Ambrose Coldharbour for wage theft and safety violations at the old cannery; the case collapsed, his family was ruined, his father died broke. He came here for Paloma, or for the sentence, or both. Emotional beat: grief that has fossilized into purpose.

chapters.title: Sunday, in Front of Everyone
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Final reunion brunch: Ambrose announces the signing date and publicly pressures Paloma. Jonah steps in, defends her with a conviction that stuns the room, and Paloma realizes the performance has stopped being one. Emotional beat: public declaration, private vertigo.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Half-Said
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Driving home, Jonah begins the rehearsed confession — 'Ten years ago, I—' — and Paloma stops him, afraid of what will break if he finishes. Emotional beat: love and dread in the same breath.

chapters.title: Kitchen Confessions
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma cooks for him for once, and in her kitchen Jonah finally tells the whole truth: who he is, what Ambrose did, why he came. She walks out. Emotional beat: devastation — the one honest thing destroys the one real thing.

chapters.title: Three Days of Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Paloma drafts the contract signature; Jonah packs to leave town. Both keep almost reaching for the phone. A neighbor mentions the cannery workers who never got their settlement — and Paloma starts pulling threads. Emotional beat: heartbreak redirected into investigation.

chapters.title: The Uncle's Ledger
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Digging through estate records, Paloma finds Ambrose falsified the vineyard's debt figures to force her hand — and an old ledger linking him to the cannery fraud Jonah witnessed. The two betrayals are the same betrayal. Emotional beat: fury with a compass.

chapters.title: Allies and Apples
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah, about to leave, is found by Paloma's aunt Marta, who suspected Ambrose for years and has documents. She brokers an uneasy truce: Jonah and Paloma together at the harvest gala, where Ambrose will sign and celebrate. Emotional beat: fragile alliance, common enemy.

chapters.title: The Harvest Gala
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The gala in full splendor; Ambrose toasts his acquisition. Paloma, in her grandmother's dress, stalls the signing while Jonah and Marta position the evidence. Emotional beat: terror worn as elegance.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Finished
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Before the assembled family, Jonah finishes the sentence he's rehearsed for a decade — naming Ambrose's crimes, his own name, his father's. Ambrose moves to discredit him; Paloma takes his hand and stands with him. Emotional beat: catharsis at maximum cost.

chapters.title: What the Family Saw
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The room fractures: cousins defect, the lawyer distances himself, Ambrose threatens litigation and loses the room. The buyout dies publicly. Paloma's inheritance is saved from the trap, not the debt. Emotional beat: victory that feels like freefall.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Pressed Like Grapes
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Investigations begin; the cannery workers' settlement is revived with Jonah's testimony. Paloma confronts what the vineyard can actually sustain — smaller, humbler, hers. Emotional beat: grief for the fantasy of rescue, relief at the truth.

chapters.title: The Offer He Didn't Plan
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Ambrose offers Jonah money to recant; Jonah refuses on the record. Paloma, having followed him, witnesses it — the man choosing justice over every easy exit, again. Emotional beat: love confirmed not by words but by refusal.

chapters.title: First Press
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The community harvest: neighbors, bistro regulars, and Marta pick the remaining fields together. Jonah and Paloma work the press side by side, and she asks him out properly — a real first date, ten years late. Emotional beat: joy earned the hard way.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Epilogue: spring, new vines in the ground, the settlement won, the bistro serving Coldharbour wine. On the cellar stairs, Jonah finally says the last unrehearsed sentence — not the confession, but the proposal of an ordinary life. She says yes. Emotional beat: quiet, unguarded happiness.
